policy.presence_standard: Inclusion means a source-controlled documentary relationship exists; it does not imply guilt, knowledge, agency, conspiracy, liability, or criminal purpose.
policy.promotion_rule: No row is promoted solely from an address book, flight log, calendar, photograph, contact list, or unverified allegation.

entities.name: Jeffrey Epstein
entities.lane: Core archive subject; banking; criminal/civil records
entities.relationship: Central subject of the archive and account holder / principal in many source records.
entities.boundary: A central index subject; individual records must still be read for exact conduct, date, and evidentiary scope.

entities.name: Ghislaine Maxwell
entities.relationship: Named in federal court records and in source material connected to Epstein.
entities.boundary: Presence in an Epstein-connected source is not interchangeable with the specific conduct adjudicated in Maxwell’s criminal case.

entities.name: JPMorgan Chase
entities.relationship: Banked Epstein and later filed suspicious-activity reports that Senate Finance reconstructed.
entities.boundary: A SAR reports suspicious activity; it does not establish that every transaction was criminal.

entities.name: Leon Black
entities.lane: Financial relationship; advisory payments; later referrals
entities.relationship: Paid Epstein for advisory work; public sources contain differing $158M and $170M aggregate totals.
entities.boundary: Large payments establish money movement and a financial relationship, not criminal purpose by themselves.

entities.name: Apollo Global Management
entities.relationship: Apollo’s Conflicts Committee commissioned the 2021 Dechert review of Black’s relationship with Epstein.
entities.boundary: The review context does not mean Apollo paid Epstein or participated in Epstein’s conduct.

entities.name: Ehud Barak
entities.relationship: Appears in a multi-year documentary record of scheduling, meetings, correspondence, and later business discussions involving Epstein.
entities.boundary: Scheduling, introductions, and correspondence do not by themselves establish purpose, agency, intelligence activity, or wrongdoing.

entities.name: Carbyne
entities.relationship: Security-technology company discussed in the 2018–2019 Barak/Qatar correspondence chain.
entities.boundary: Discussion or a pitch does not establish a completed transaction, deployment, or government adoption.

entities.name: Jabor Al Thani
entities.relationship: Introduced by Epstein to Barak in the documented Qatar/Carbyne correspondence chain.
entities.boundary: An introduction and follow-up correspondence do not establish agreement, procurement, or improper purpose.

entities.name: Financial Trust Company, Inc.
entities.relationship: Appears in bank statements and transaction records involving investments and the 2012 Black Family Partners asset sale.
entities.boundary: Ownership or investment activity does not by itself establish operational control or downstream conduct.

entities.name: Black Family Partners, L.P.
entities.relationship: Counterparty in the documented November 2012 purchase of Financial Trust assets, including ESWW-related interests.
entities.boundary: The transaction record establishes the sale and receipt; it does not, by itself, identify the ultimate source of every dollar used for the purchase.

entities.name: Environmental Solutions Worldwide (ESWW)
entities.relationship: Public-company investment held by Financial Trust and later included in the 2012 Black Family Partners transaction.
entities.boundary: Investment and share ownership do not establish operational control or causation for later government use of the company’s technology.

entities.name: Jes Staley
entities.relationship: Appears in JPMorgan records and later litigation concerning the bank’s relationship with Epstein.
entities.boundary: A banker-client relationship and internal references must be separated from any specific knowledge or conduct claim.

entities.name: Jorge Amador
entities.relationship: Forensic accountant whose June 16, 2023 expert report analyzed Epstein-related JPMorgan accounts and transaction patterns.
entities.boundary: His characterizations of suspiciousness and legitimate business purpose are expert opinions, not judicial findings.

entities.name: Darren Indyke
entities.relationship: Appears in Epstein-related legal and financial execution records and later transaction reviews.
entities.boundary: Record presence and execution of transactions do not establish knowledge of unrelated criminal conduct.

entities.name: Alexander Acosta
entities.relationship: U.S. Attorney whose office negotiated and approved the 2007 non-prosecution agreement; OPR later reviewed the decision.
entities.boundary: OPR found poor judgment but did not find professional misconduct or evidence of a corrupt or impermissible motive.

entities.name: A. Marie Villafaña
entities.relationship: Lead prosecutor whose emails and later statement anchor key prosecution and victim-notification chronology.
entities.boundary: Her later statement is retrospective and should be distinguished from contemporaneous records.

entities.name: Jeffrey Sloman
entities.relationship: First Assistant U.S. Attorney who sent the December 7, 2007 “Hold the letter” instruction.
entities.boundary: The native email establishes the hold instruction; it does not identify the person Sloman later recalled speaking to.

entities.name: DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility
entities.relationship: Conducted the official review of the 2006–2008 federal Epstein investigation and NPA process.
entities.boundary: OPR is a retrospective official review; its findings do not substitute for the underlying primary records where those records are available.

entities.name: Metropolitan Correctional Center, New York
entities.relationship: Federal detention facility where Epstein was held and died in August 2019.
entities.boundary: Documented custodial failures do not, by themselves, establish third-party criminality in the death.

entities.name: Government of the U.S. Virgin Islands
entities.relationship: Brought civil litigation involving Epstein-related banking activity and entered a 2023 settlement with Leon Black.
entities.boundary: Civil allegations and settlements must be kept separate from criminal findings and admissions.
